OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): All THREE divergences this entry stacked are closed at once. BeatDown.cs:26 is `.ToList().StableShuffle(Rng.Shuffle).Take(3)`, and `player.stable_shuffled_cards` is exactly that verb: it SORTS first by CardModel.CompareTo (ListExtensions.cs:22-31), which is what stops the pick depending on discard-pile order, and only then Fisher-Yates on the named **Shuffle** stream. colorless_skills.py calls it in place of `ctx.combat._rng.shuffle(candidates)`. Note this is StableShuffle, NOT the TakeRandom/UnstableShuffle its five siblings in this batch use -- the two verbs differ by that sort, and using the wrong one here would reintroduce the order dependence.  Pinned by test/test_take_random_streams.py, which gives every named accessor its own Random and asserts the site advanced the one its C# names and did NOT touch the shared `combat._rng`.  The auto-play still advances CombatTargets, which is correct (CardCmd.cs:77). NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: The candidate FILTER is faithful (`c.Type == CardType.Attack && !c.Keywords.Contains(CardKeyword.Unplayable)` on the discard pile, BeatDown.cs:26, == `c.card_type == CardType.ATTACK and c.is_playable` over `ctx.player.discard_pile`), and so is the per-card auto-play with the loop's early exit. THE SELECTION IS NOT. C# does `.ToList().StableShuffle(Owner.RunState.Rng.Shuffle).Take(IntValue)`: StableShuffle first SORTS the list (`list2.Sort()`, ListExtensions.cs:22-31 -- by CardModel.CompareTo, i.e. the canonical UPPERCASE-id order noted in the seed facts) so the result no longer depends on discard-pile order, THEN Fisher-Yates shuffles it on the named **Shuffle** stream. The sim calls `ctx.combat._rng.shuffle(candidates)` (colorless_skills.py:113): the unseeded shared `random.Random`, not `ctx.combat.combat_rng.shuffle` (the accessor exists -- combat_rng.py:17,50), with NO pre-sort, and Python's `random.shuffle` is a different Fisher-Yates variant. Three independent divergences stack: wrong stream, missing stabilising sort (so identical discard contents in a different order pick different cards), and a different draw sequence. Observable: under a string-seeded parity run Beat Down auto-plays a different set of attacks than the recorded run and desyncs the Shuffle stream for every later reshuffle. LIVE -- Beat Down is a ported Rare colorless Skill and the Shuffle parity stream is already wired (`CombatRng.parity`, combat_rng.py:41-46). REGRESSION TEST: `test/test_rng_tripwire.py:33` (`test_no_wrong_stream_draws_in_random_run`, 20 seeded full runs) is the standing gate for this whole family. It wraps `RunState.rng` and asserts ZERO in-combat draws on it; `CombatState` receives that same object as `self._rng` (run.py:1146-1148, combat.py:88), so a `ctx.combat._rng` draw taken from inside a card's `on_play` is recorded and fails the gate -- verified by playing this family's shape under a `Tripwire` and getting a hit at the `card.on_play` frame (combat.py:490). The gate is green today, so these 20 seeds never reach this card's draw; routing the site to the named `combat_rng` accessor is verified by keeping it green.

guards.what: target selection for AnyEnemy attacks: C# rolls `Rng.CombatTargets.NextItem(CombatState.HittableEnemies)` in BeatDown itself and passes it to AutoPlay; the sim lets `auto_play_card` roll (BeatDown.cs:32-40)
guards.issue: Closed 2026-08-03. FIXED, and the DORMANT label it carried was WRONG -- refuted by execution, not by argument. The divergence is real and is exactly as recorded: BeatDown.cs:32-40 rolls `Rng.CombatTargets.NextItem(CombatState.HittableEnemies)` ITSELF and passes the result into `CardCmd.AutoPlay`, while `AutoPlay` tests the Unplayable keyword (CardCmd.cs:58-62) and `Hook.ShouldPlay` (:63-72) BEFORE its own `target == null` roll (:73-81) -- so Beat Down's draw is spent whether or not the play then survives the veto, and the sim's roll (inside `auto_play_card`, AFTER the veto, combat.py) was not. THE DORMANCY CLAIM ('no such preventer is ported that fires on an auto-played Attack') WAS FALSE. Census of all 8 ported `should_play_card` implementers: FIVE can veto an auto-played Attack. Three do so unconditionally, checking neither `auto_play` nor card type -- `SlothPower` (powers.py, `_cards_played_this_turn < amount`), reached as a Knowledge Demon curse (cards/knowledge_curses.py); `VelvetChoker` (relics/velvet_choker.py, same shape), a Darv event reward (events/darv.py); and `NormalityCard` (cards/normality.py), whose own comment already said the game blocks an auto-played card in that window. Two more veto an Attack that carries their affliction, and neither affliction is type-restricted: `RingingPower` (afflicts any affliction-free card, then vetoes once any play has STARTED this turn -- and Beat Down's own play has) and `ChainsOfBindingPower` (Bound). Only three cannot: `ClashCard` and `EnthralledCard` exempt auto-plays explicitly, and `SmoggyPower` afflicts SKILLS only. MEASURED before the fix, three AnyEnemy Attacks in the discard pile (one CombatTargets draw each in C#): baseline 3 draws; with SlothPower(1) the sim drew 1; with Velvet Choker at its cap, 0. Under seed parity that is a stream desync for the rest of the combat. FIX: `BeatDownCard.on_play` (cards/colorless_skills.py) now rolls the target itself and passes `target_idx` in, mirroring BeatDown.cs:32-40, including the empty-HittableEnemies arm (CardCmd.cs:78-81, card spent unplayed). Beat Down is the ONLY pre-roll caller in the game source (`grep -rn 'CombatTargets.NextItem' src/` returns this site and CardCmd.cs's own two), so no other `auto_play_card` caller needed touching and this is not a partial port. Pinned by test/test_take_random_streams.py::test_beat_down_spends_a_combat_targets_draw_even_when_the_play_is_vetoed, verified to FAIL (1 != 3) against the pre-fix tree.

guards.rationale: `auto_play_card` removes the card from whichever of hand/draw/discard/exhaust holds it before resolving (combat.py:526-535) and routes it through `_resolve_card_play`, matching CardCmd.AutoPlay's pile handling. Beat Down itself is in the discard-pile limbo while this runs (combat.py:452-454) but is a Skill, so it is never its own candidate.
